## Summary

**MOVE2** (Move two): Move a pair.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `Source pair → destination pair` |
| Syntax | `MOVE2 <ea>,b:c`<br>`MOVE2 b:c,<ea>` |
| Short | Move a pair. |
| Description | Moves from or to memory two registers. Size byte, word or long. |
| Condition codes | are taken from b, the first. |

### Condition codes

| X | N | Z | V | C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| – | * | * | 0 | 0 |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–8 | `00001110` |
| 1 | 7–6 | Size |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | B |
| 2 | 11 | d |
| 2 | 10 | `0` |
| 2 | 9–6 | C |
| 2 | 5–0 | `010001` |

- S=Size 0=byte, 1=word, 2= long.
- B & C: data or address-register.
- direction d=0: &lt;ea&gt;,b else b,&lt;ea&gt;

### Example

```asm
    move2.w    (a0),d2:d3
```

- ea (a0) memory content where a0 points to

```text
01 23 45 67 89 AB CD EF
Result:
b d2 & d3: .. .. .. .. .. .. 01 23
           .. .. .. .. .. .. 45 67
```

### Notes

- movz2 extends unsigned, movem extends signed.
- &lt;ea&gt; must refer to memory, else unexpected result.
- move2 is not correct on V2

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no MOVE2. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DO use a memory `<ea>`: other modes give unexpected results.
- DON'T rely on MOVE2 on V2 cores: the manual says it is not correct there.
